content: Photo Credit: StarWars.com Kevin Smith penned a Marvel Comics story in which the Avengers, X-Men, and the Fantastic Four cross over with characters from Star Wars: A New Hope —a first for the two pop-culture behemoths. However, it seems the creator of Masters of the Universe: Revelations isn’t done with the idea just yet. Bleeding Cool reported that Smith already has plans for a sequel. Since Hope Assembles was meant to celebrate A New Hope’s 50th anniversary, Smith hopes the opportunity will come again with The Empire Strikes Back’s 50th anniversary. Kevin Smith was further intrigued by the idea, thanks to Rafael Albuquerque’s cover, which depicted Darth Vader with the Infinity Gauntlet. Regarding that, he said, “Once I saw that image, I was like, ‘Oh, that needs to happen… it will play an integral part in the 50th anniversary Empire Strikes Back recrossover.” Regarding his hopes for a sequel, Smith said, “Hopefully we get to do this again with The Empire Strikes Back…The thing that would make that inevitable, impossible not to do would be if fans come in and you all sell, you know, millions of copies of these and then we’ll do it again if we get that right.” What do we know about Marvel’s upcoming crossover with Star Wars? The crossover, billed as “A Galaxy Far, Far Away Meets the World Outside Your Window”, sees the Star Wars franchise crossover with heroes of the Marvel universe. The crossover is meant to celebrate Star Wars’ 50th anniversary, with the first issue hitting shelves on January 13, 2027. The five-issue series will focus on the events of New Hope, unfolding on Earth-616 due to a “reality-altering spell.” Kevin Smith is writing the story, with art by David Marquez. The second issue is scheduled to hit shelves on February 17, 2027. Reports say the event will not be an Elseworld story. The storyline will feature the Avengers, the X-Men, and the Fantastic Four meeting Luke, Han, and Leia, while Darth Vader allies himself with Doctor Doom. Originally reported on SuperHeroHype . content: Photo Credit - IO Interactive Lenny Kravitz ‘s 007 First Light character will return in an exciting crossover event, and further details about the collaboration have been revealed. IO Interactive has introduced Kravitz as Bawma in a new Elusive Target mission for Hitman World of Assassination . The character is playable from November 26 until December 24, 2026, for free as part of the Free Demo for new players and in the game for players who already own Hitman World of Assassination for a limited time. The new Elusive Target mission will feature Kravitz’s voiceover as the Pirate King Bawma. The Grammy winner shared in a recent statement, “Bawma is such a fun and interesting character to portray, so I was excited to step back into a new world with him for 007 First Light. Seeing Bawma team up with Agent 47 is something I think fans of both games are going to love.” In this latest mission, Agent 47 is deployed to Ambrose Island on the instruction of Bawma. After tracking him down through the island’s ruins and jungles, 47 realizes that the mission involves something far more valuable than a simple target. Three of Bawma’s rogue lieutenants stand guard over something they will not let go so easily. The new Elusive Target comes with more free content for Hitman players Players who own Hitman World of Assassination or have access to Ambrose Island and complete The Mutiny before its December 24 expiration will retain permanent access to the Arcade version of the mission and its Special Assignment for free. Additionally, the game is launching a brand-new roadmap, bringing fresh and returning content for players to enjoy. These include a new Elusive Target, a new Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop, and an IOI Account reward. Two fan-favorite Elusive Targets and two seasonal events are also returning. As with all Elusive Targets, this mission will be removed from the game when it expires on December 24, 2026. title: Maddie Ziegler’s Netflix Christmas Movie Has Surprising Horror Roots

content: (Photo Credit: Bettina Strauss/Netflix © 2026) Christina Lauren, the writing duo of Christina Hobbs and Lauren Billings, spoke with ComingSoon’s Tyler Treese about their book In a Holidaze becoming a Netflix movie starring Maddie Ziegler and Rob Lowe. They discussed the film’s unique time loop, how it was inspired by a horror movie, and more. It begins streaming on December 2, 2026. “After making a romantic mistake of epic proportions, a directionless twenty-something finds herself trapped in a holiday time-loop, forced to relive the same Christmas at her family’s cabin until she discovers what truly makes her happy,” says the official synopsis. Tyler Treese: Christina, I always love seeing if authors got to visit the set any. So did you get to actually check it out? Because the cabin is such a character in the story of In a Holidaze, so I can’t imagine what it was like if you got to see it brought to life. Christina Hobbs: Yes, we did get to visit the set. We were there for two days in March. And when we walked in, I immediately started crying because it was this huge cabin, life-size cabin, and it was so beautiful. It was every detail. As soon as I saw the Christmas tree and the stockings with their names on them, I just started crying. And the family photos up on the stairs, even the books on the shelf. There was a Danielle Steel book on the shelf, and it was just so perfectly curated. Yeah. Lauren, I was curious how it felt watching the film and seeing Mae brought to life by Maddie Ziegler. She’s so charismatic in this film. So how was it seeing this character that you two crafted brought to life on the screen? Lauren Billings: Yeah, I mean, she’s perfect. And it’s sort of indescribable because you write a character and you sort of have an idea of who they are, and that’s why when people ask us, “Who would you cast as this character in this book?” or whatever, we can’t really ever think of it because they’re their own person in our head. But she is Mae. She was perfect. She’s vulnerable. She’s loving. She’s loyal. She’s funny. She’s all of these things, and she captures that so perfectly. And also, Maddie is just a really, really wonderful human being. I don’t know, I feel so lucky that we got her for Mae because nobody else could have done it as well. Hobbs: Yeah, she is Mae. Billings: Yeah. Christina, I was interested in In a Holidaze because it’s a multiple-day time loop rather than just one repeating day, like Groundhog Day. What did you like most about that convention? Because we really get to see the ramifications of the actions, which I thought was really interesting. Christina Hobbs: Well, so everybody thinks that it’s like Groundhog Day, but really the inspiration came from Happy Death Day, which is one of our favorite movies. It’s so clever. And I love the thing that she can go a little bit further, and that’s how she knows, or she thinks that she knows, that she’s doing something right. It’s like, “Oh, I made it to the 22nd. I made it to the 23rd.” And they were able to do it so much better, I think, than we were in the book because we get to see her reaction, where in the book, we have to tell the reader everything that’s happening. They were so smart about how they did it. Lauren, we get introduced to a lot of characters right off the bat in In a Holidaze. I was a bit concerned about remembering everybody, but by the end, I was charmed and liked everybody. What’s most difficult when you have such an ensemble and making sure nobody seems unneeded and everybody has their little moments? Lauren Billings: Yeah, so we’ve written series where it started with one couple, and by the last book in the series, we have five couples, and everybody has their favorite, and the readers are gonna wanna see everybody on the same page. And it’s just really hard to manage. This book, because it felt like this chosen family was sort of the scaffold around Andrew and Mae’s love story, it didn’t feel hard to write because everybody kind of lent a different level of support to them as a couple. I think when we visited set, we hadn’t realized how hard that would be to manage from a production standpoint because it’s so many people on set. There’s like 11 cast members that are always together. But they did it so beautifully. I mean, I think that, like you said, you can be worried at the beginning that you’re not gonna be able to remember everybody, but everybody has such a distinct personality, and they’re so dimensional, and they’re so beautifully created and also acted, brought to life by these actors. I don’t know, I think that it’s done so perfectly. It’s really impressive. Thanks to Christina Lauren for taking the time to talk about In a Holidaze. content: Photo Credit: Paramount Pictures Daniel Radcliffe ‘s latest animated fairy-tale adventure is finding a large audience on Netflix . The film puts a playful spin on the Cinderella story, giving its characters unexpected roles. With a star-packed voice cast and a kingdom in trouble, the movie offers fans a different kind of magical ride. Steps claims No. 1 position on Netflix charts According to FlixPatrol , Steps has climbed to the top of Netflix’s U.S. Top 10 movies chart, moving ahead of titles such as Guarding Stars, Rob Lowe: The Outsider, All for Christmas, Insidious: Out of the Further, Obsession and Primetime Preacher$. Daniel Radcliffe voices Prince Charming, but the story gives the spotlight to Cinderella’s stepsisters, Lilith and Margot. Ali Wong voices Lilith, while Stephanie Hsu plays Margot. Amanda Seyfried lends her voice to Cinderella, and Bette Midler plays the Fairy Godmother. Nikki Glaser voices Priscilla, Peter Dinklage plays Roderick, and Young Mazino voices Gef. Damian Priest also joins the cast as Cracktor. Lilith is done playing second fiddle to Cinderella, so she makes a reckless grab for the Fairy Godmother’s wand. The stunt throws the royal ball into chaos and hands Priscilla the perfect chance to take control and chase after Prince Charming. Now Lilith must team up with Cinderella to pull the kingdom out of the trouble. Their rescue mission brings them face-to-face with motorcycle-riding trolls, a menacing man-nanny and the nightmare-inducing Screaming Woods. Directors Alyce Tzue and John Ripa reshape the familiar tale around sisterhood and belonging. Tzue told TUDUM that she wanted to tell a story for people who “felt like they didn’t belong.” Wong also welcomed the chance to play someone driven by resentment. “I thought it was a fun challenge to play a character so full of resentment, who wasn’t born as some genetic masterpiece, and who had to work through all of that,” she said. Steps also has an 81% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes , a 74% audience score, and a 6.7 rating on IMDb . content: Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures Godzilla x Kong: Supernova writer Dave Callaham recently shared his thoughts on how the MonsterVerse has changed since his first involvement with the franchise. Comparing the 2014 film Godzilla with the upcoming sequel, he noted the significant shift in the series’ approach. His comments also reveal how different the creative process was when he returned to write the latest chapter. Dave Callaham compares his two MonsterVerse experiences Dave Callaham has described how his approach to the MonsterVerse changed between his work on the 2014 Godzilla film and the upcoming Godzilla x Kong: Supernova. The screenwriter discussed the contrast between the projects during an appearance on the Escape Hatch podcast , explaining that his return to the franchise was a very different creative experience from his first time working on it. Callaham spoke about writing Godzilla x Kong: Supernova, the next chapter in the MonsterVerse franchise, and expressed satisfaction with the finished script. “I also wrote next year’s Godzilla Kong installment. It’s called Godzilla x Kong: Supernova. Which I think is pretty good for one of those movies. Make of that what you will, I’m pretty happy about it,” he said. He then reflected on the difference between the two MonsterVerse projects that he’s worked on, particularly the shift in how the franchise approaches realism. Callaham worked on the 2014 Godzilla, which aimed for a more realistic portrayal of the giant monster and the world around it. Returning to the series for Supernova meant adapting to a franchise that has since moved further away from that approach. “I had a real fun time coming back to the MonsterVerse after working on the 2014 movie, which we tried to make very realistic. And now, uh, those movies are not very realistic anymore, so that was a fun switch,” Callaham added. The upcoming film’s cast includes Kaitlyn Dever as Jesse Portman, Dan Stevens as Trapper, Jack O’Connell as John Portman, and Delroy Lindo as Conway. It is set to hit theaters on March 26, 2027. content: Photo Credit: Lionsgate Fans of Simon Pegg’s comedy films have received an exciting update from the actor in a recent interview. The news comes more than a decade after the last installment and could bring a fourth movie to the beloved Cornetto trilogy . In an interview with LADbible Ireland, Pegg was asked about the possibility of reuniting with Edgar Wright for a fourth movie. The actor confirmed that the project is in its early stages, saying, “It’s in the very, very early stages. Yeah. But, but yeah, absolutely.” View this post on Instagram Pegg further revealed, “Edgar and I are sort of talking about it at the moment. We’ve got a Zoom call tomorrow about, you know, we’re sort of fleshing out something at the moment.” However, the 56-year-old actor did not disclose any details about the potential fourth installment or its storyline. The Cornetto trilogy began with three films that became cult favorites The Three Flavors Cornetto trilogy began in 2004 with Shaun of the Dead, a horror comedy directed by Wright and co-written by him and Pegg. The film follows Pegg’s Shaun, an ordinary man whose life takes an unexpected turn when a zombie outbreak hits London. Alongside his best friend Ed, played by Nick Frost , Shaun struggles to protect his loved ones while navigating the chaos. The trilogy’s second film, Hot Fuzz, was released in 2007, shifting the focus from horror comedy to a police action comedy. Pegg stars as Nicholas Angel, a highly skilled London police officer who is transferred to the quiet village of Sandford. However, a series of suspicious deaths soon raises questions about the seemingly peaceful community. Frost plays Danny Butterman, Angel’s enthusiastic new partner. The trilogy concluded in 2013 with The World’s End, which shifted the focus to science fiction. Pegg stars as Gary King, a man who convinces his childhood friends to return to their hometown and complete a pub crawl they failed to finish in their youth. However, their reunion takes an unexpected turn when the group discovers that something strange has happened to the town’s residents. content: Photo Credit - Apple TV Milo Manheim recalls the unexpected moment he learned he would play Flynn Rider in Disney ‘s live-action Tangled . The actor revealed that he had received the casting news shortly before the announcement went public. He also shared his immediate reaction and explained how excited he was to join the upcoming adaptation. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly , Manheim clarified that he had not been keeping the casting news a secret for months. He explained, “I found out 10 minutes before the news was released that I’d be playing Flynn.” He recalled, “My skin was like tingling that day,” and added that he felt “flooded with dopamine and love and everything.” View this post on Instagram Why playing Flynn Rider is such a dream come true for Milo Manheim Manheim’s excitement also comes from his connection to the original Disney film. The actor expressed his admiration for the animated film and emphasized that he wants to respect its legacy while stepping into Flynn’s shoes. He said, “I want to really honor this movie and this role.” Sharing his enthusiasm, Manheim added, “I love, I love Tangled, so here we go, adventure of a lifetime.” For Manheim, the opportunity is particularly meaningful because he gets to be part of a story he already loves. The actor will star opposite Teagan Croft , who will play Rapunzel. Kathryn Hahn will play Mother Gothel. Diego Luna has also joined the cast in a currently undisclosed role. Patrick and Hugo McPherson will portray the Stabbington brothers. Michael Gracey, who previously directed The Greatest Showman, is helming the live-action film. Jennifer Kaytin Robinson and Michael Montemayor are writing the screenplay, while Kristin Burr is producing the project. Lucy Kitada serves as an executive producer. Disney’s original Tangled premiered in 2010 and featured Mandy Moore as Rapunzel and Zachary Levi as Flynn Rider. The animated musical follows the pair as they embark on an adventure that takes Rapunzel beyond the tower where she has spent most of her life. title: Dune: Part Three’s Reported Budget Sets New Benchmark for Villeneuve’s Sci-Fi Saga
summary: Denis Villeneuve’s Dune universe is getting one of its biggest productions yet The post Dune: Part Three’s Reported Budget Sets New Benchmark for Villeneuve’s Sci-Fi Saga appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit - Warner Bros. Pictures Denis Villeneuve ‘s Dune universe is getting one of its biggest productions yet. The reported price tag for Dune: Part Three puts the final chapter ahead of its two predecessors, making it the most expensive entry in his sci-fi saga. According to The New York Times , Legendary Entertainment and Warner Bros. reportedly spent about $200 million on the film’s production, excluding marketing. Dune: Part Three draws from Frank Herbert’s novel Dune Messiah and follows Paul Atreides after his rise to power. The story takes place nearly two decades after Dune: Part Two, with Timothée Chalamet returning as the emperor. Zendaya reprises her role as Chani, while Robert Pattinson joins the cast as a character plotting against Paul. Anya Taylor-Joy also returns as Alia. How does Dune: Part 3’s budget compare with previous Dune movies? The reported $200 million budget makes Dune: Part Three the most expensive film in Villeneuve’s trilogy. The 2021 Dune reportedly cost $165 million , while Dune: Part Two had a $190 million production budget. The new film is $35 million more expensive than the first movie and $10 million more expensive than the second. Its budget has grown by about 21% since the original film. The earlier movies also built a strong theatrical record for the franchise. According to The Numbers , Dune earned around $430 million worldwide. Dune: Part Two collected roughly $715 million globally, grossing about $285 million more than the first film. It also opened to $82.5 million in North America, more than double the original’s $41 million debut. Dune: Part Two earned more than three times its reported production budget worldwide, setting a strong box-office benchmark for the third film. Dune: Part Three is scheduled to arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026, alongside Avengers: Doomsday . Fans have nicknamed the double release DunesDay, just like Barbenheimer in 2023. content: Photo Credit - Netflix Danny Boyle has shared his views on speculation about Jack O’Connell ‘s involvement in the upcoming James Bond project. According to the filmmaker, O’Connell could have been a “great” 007, if not for Robert Pattinson . Moreover, Boyle also shared his insights on who could play the next Bond villain. During his appearance on Alchemy with Anthony Mason, Boyle was asked about his 2019 comment suggesting that Pattinson would make a good James Bond. The filmmaker praised the Twilight actor’s talent and said, “He’s a terrific actor, but we have an actor in this [Ink]; Jack O’Connell would have been a great Bond as well.” Boyle further added, “I can see they’re beginning in all this talk. They’re talking about Jack O’Connell as a possible villain,” hinting that the Sinners star could be a part of Robert Pattinson’s upcoming 007 movie. Boyle and O’Connell recently collaborated on Ink, an upcoming biographical drama about Rupert Murdoch and editor Larry Lamb. content: Photo Credit - Warner Bros. Pictures I Am Legend director Francis Lawrence has shared his candid thoughts on how the 2007 film ended. Lawrence called the movie’s ending “a bit of failure” in a recent podcast. Speaking on the Team Deakins podcast, Lawrence revisited the 2007 film and discussed how the creatures turned out on screen. Looking back, he felt they were too similar to humans and believed their design should have been different. “I’m really proud of the first hour of that movie,” he shared of the I Am Legend film, which focused more on Neville’s story and his survival. “But the last 40 minutes, where the creatures end up becoming a big part of it, I think it’s a bit of a failure, honestly, and we just didn’t approach it the way that we should have and could have.” Lawrence then revisited the original ending, in which Will Smith’s character fails to find a cure and leaves Anna to the monsters. “That was our original ending. It tested horribly twice. Twice,” the filmmaker revealed. He added that the team shot a replacement ending three months before the film’s release, which eventually became the theatrical ending audiences saw in 2007. Which ending will I Am Legend 2 stick with? The Will Smith-led film featured an alternate ending with its DVD release. In the theatrical version, Neville, played by Smith, gives Anna and Ethan the cure, hides them in a secure compartment, and sacrifices himself with a grenade to stop the attackers. In the alternate version, Neville realizes that the infected are trying to rescue their own and returns the female companion he captured for his experiments. As a result, he gets to survive. The sequel is expected to continue on this version. Akiva Goldsman is writing the follow-up with Smith and Michael B. Jordan set to star. Steven Caple Jr. was eyed to direct, though Goldsman said in September that the project faces “a series of obstacles.” The untitled sequel does not yet have a release date. As The Hollywood Reporter reported, StudioCanal and Mediatoon Distribution have reached an agreement to bring three animated movies from the franchise back to audiences. The legacy of Asterix’s classic animated movies The agreement covers Asterix the Gaul, Asterix and Cleopatra, and Asterix Conquers Rome. The release plans also include a collector’s DVD box set featuring the three films. It will arrive in France during the 2026 holiday season and in Germany in spring 2027. Viewers in Poland and the Netherlands will also be able to watch the films on video-on-demand platforms. The initiative will help celebrate the franchise’s history over the coming years. Asterix Conquers Rome will mark its 50th anniversary, while Asterix the Gaul will celebrate its 60th anniversary in 2028. Created by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo , Asterix remains one of Europe’s most successful cultural franchises. The comic books have sold more than 400 million copies worldwide, and the animated films have introduced generations of viewers to the adventures of the indomitable Gauls. The partnership aims to bring these classics to new audiences while giving longtime fans another chance to experience them on the big screen. content: Photo Credit: Marvel The Fantastic Four: First Steps movie appeared to have a successful run in theaters; however, its box office earnings did not meet Marvel Studios ‘ expectations. New financial details about the 2025 superhero movie suggest its performance goes beyond its worldwide gross. According to a Forbes report released on November 25, Disney’s financial filings show that The Fantastic Four: First Steps exceeded its production budget. The movie earned around $521.9 million worldwide, but Disney’s ticket sales did not cover its production costs. The report estimates it lost about $336.7 million at the box office, even before marketing expenses. That said, it is important to note that a movie’s worldwide box office total is not the same as the money its studio receives. Since theaters keep a share of ticket sales, Disney did not receive the full $521.9 million worldwide earnings. Moreover, according to the source, if the money were split 50-50, the studio would have received around $260.9 million—still less than the reported production cost. The Fantastic Four: First Steps’ production costs tell a different story Although Forbes reported that The Fantastic Four: First Steps exceeded its original production budget, Disney’s financial filings tell a different story. According to Disney’s financial controller, Tracy Bermingham, the company spent another $141.5 million that year, bringing the movie’s total production cost to $371.1 million. Additionally, before the movie’s theatrical run, the production budget was reported to be above $200 million. However, the final cost was much higher, especially during post-production. But because the movie was shot at Pinewood Studios in the United Kingdom, where film productions can receive rebates through the government’s Audio-Visual Expenditure Credit scheme, Disney received $73.5 million, bringing the total expenditure down to $297.6 million. A further breakdown of production costs reported $26.8 million for staff wages, excluding freelancers, contractors, and temporary staff who worked on the movie’s production. content: (Photo Credit: Netflix) Lori Loughlin ‘s Thanksgiving message came with a hilarious dig at her Full House character. The actress shared a holiday greeting that poked fun at her sitcom character, Aunt Becky , and her diet advice. In her Instagram post, she joked with her followers, “Don’t listen to Aunt Becky. Happy Thanksgiving, everyone!!” The caption accompanied a clip of Loughlin silently digging into a slice of pumpkin pie topped with a generous helping of whipped cream. Meanwhile, what appeared to be her dialogue from a 1990 episode of the sitcom played in the background. In the video, Loughlin’s character offers a list of diet-friendly foods to Candace Cameron Bure’s D.J., who is trying to lose weight. This happened in the episode “Shape Up.” As Becky advises D.J. to avoid junk food, Loughlin playfully ignores her character’s advice by taking a bite of another sweet: a brownie! View this post on Instagram Full House episode that made Aunt Becky’s diet advice so memorable Aunt Becky’s diet advice appeared in the 1990 Full House episode “Shape Up.” Loughlin’s Rebecca “Aunt Becky” Donaldson offers diet advice to D.J. Tanner, listing supposedly healthy foods before warning her about junk food. Becky tells D.J. that all she has to do to lose a couple of pounds is eat sensibly. She then lists several foods, saying, “You can have boiled fish, lean chicken without the skin, fresh fruits, delicious steamed vegetables, a nice whole grain pasta with a light tomato sauce and just a sprinkling of Parmesan cheese.” She is then interrupted by D.J. as she quipped, “Becky, I’m trying to keep my mind off of food,” to which Loughlin’s character continued, “Sorry. The most important thing is just to keep the junk food out of the house.” John Stamos, who played Becky’s husband, Jesse “Uncle Jesse” Katsopolis, replied to the post, commenting, “Funny.” Other fans called the post “brilliant,” while some echoed Jesse’s signature phrase, “Have mercy!” Earlier this year, Bure reflected on Full House’s legacy in an interview with Woman’s World. She said, “It’s been a dream to have been a part of a show that has a real, true legacy. It’s never been off the air in over 35 years. Full House means so much to so many people. I was on the show from 10 to 18, and you never know how something’s gonna go and what it’s gonna mean to people. So when I look back, I have so much appreciation.” Full House spawned a Netflix sequel series called Fuller House, which aired from 2016 to 2020. content: Photo Credit: HBO Max The creators of Netflix’s Dark are reuniting for a new thriller, which has now released its first teaser trailer. HBO Max has released the teaser for Sonnental . It is an upcoming mystery thriller series that comes from Jantje Friese and Baran bo Odar, who spearheaded Netflix’s cult sci-fi mystery Dark, which ran for three seasons from 2017 to 2020. Sonnental is a six-part series that stars Lisa Vicari as Anja Vogler, a profiler assigned to investigate a gruesome murder in her old hometown. As the body count rises, Vogler begins to notice an eerie link between the murders and disturbing tales from Struwwelpeter, a German children’s book meant to warn children against misbehaving. Check out the Sonnental teaser trailer below. What do we see in the Sonnental trailer? The official teaser for Sonnental begins with a chilling shot of a dark forest road before cutting to multiple unsettling vignettes of grim moments from the show. Throughout the opening beats, a voiceover by a child reads, “Der Friederich, der Friederich, Das war ein arger Wüterich!” the opening couplet from the story “The Story of Wicked Frederick” from Struwwelpeter. Joining Lisa Vicari, Sonnental also stars Peter Kurth as investigator Norbert Troschitz. The series’ supporting cast includes Jan Friedrichsen as Anja’s son Max, Iris Böhm as Anja’s mother Kerstin, Merlin Rose, Maria Simon, Mišel Matičević, and Stipe Erceg. Vicari has previously featured in Netflix’s Dark. Her credits also include Hijack, Django, Tatort, Isi & Ossi, and more. Meanwhile, Kurth has appeared in the Netflix miniseries Inventing Anna and the police procedural show Criminal: Germany. He portrayed Hermann Kafka in the 2025 biographical drama film Franz. Sonnental is a German HBO Max original created by Matija Dragojević, who co-wrote the series with Bob Konrad. All six episodes are scheduled to premiere on HBO Max in March 2027, although an exact release date has yet to be announced.
